title: A builder resolves a merge that conflicts in a test file, and a check proves no test was lost
why: Lane doing-needs-live-lane (#1340, F3) merged main and hit conflicts in test and product files. A builder may not commit a merge that touches a test file, and a test-author may not commit product files, so no role could land it; the lane orchestrator committed it itself (head 36c08a00e). Source: coordinator 17:50 CST Nov 6.
note: Ruling R31 (owner 11:02 CST Nov 11, box answer under plan item 3.8: "as long as it's well defined and doesn't create loop holes builder plus check definitely seems ideal no?"; retrospective relay 11:04 CST, plan b5f2551). Changes page items 420 a and 437 a in decision builders-cannot-edit-tests. The check reads test files with the language's parser and refuses at the merge commit: (1) a test case from either parent missing, renamed or moved; (2) a case body that differs from both parents; (3) a skip or expected-fail mark, or a changed assertion, that neither parent had; (4) new test content neither parent had (stays test-author work); (5) a test-config or mutation-test change beyond one parent's version. Each case is shown red before the route opens; the builder-test refusal stays until then. A guard change: rounds and net value apply. Earlier incident (Nov 7 12:30-13:05 CST, lane cs-revive-ready): no single role could commit a merge whose conflicts span test and product files (#1143, #1175, #1179, #1166, #1317). Stage 3, item 3.8. Open clash (#2590 round 1, haiku, 11:17 CST): case 5 lets a merge take one parent's mutation test, against item 447 a (a builder never changes the three mutation tests); sent to the retrospective to name 447 a or narrow case 5. Folded in: step mixed-merge-no-role (sighting #2083, Nov 8). Related: mixed-merge-resolver (closed #1683, a named-role design R31 replaces) and orchestrator-mixed-merge-refused (an orchestrator's own merge edits; stays separate). Also seen on #1099 and #1318 (coordinator). Interim route: re-cut by file (coordinator pick 08:00 CST).
